open_points.subject: prepare_request credential header
open_points.text: prepare_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] The headers sent are exactly: one host header, which is the instance's required header named host compared without regard to case, sent verbatim, when one exists, otherwise the authority of base_url exactly as written; accept-encoding with value identity; the instance's other required headers with their values verbatim; the credential header; and, with a body, content-type and content-length; the HTTP client adds no other header, no user agent and no connection header.
open_points.other_text: - ResolvedCredential fields (exact, no others exist): header_name: str, header_value: str
open_points.question: Which passage must change, or how is the requirement reconciled when header_name is Host: sending it in addition to the prescribed host header violates “one host header,” while using one header for both cannot in general preserve both the prescribed host value and the credential value?

open_points.question: Which passage must change, or how is an arbitrary string containing an invalid HTTP field name, a control character, or an unsendable header value to be sent as the credential header when no credential-header validation or corresponding PreSendFailure is permitted?

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request response ceiling
open_points.text: the response body is counted after transfer decoding and read at most to the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant
open_points.other_text: a longer body being over the ceiling.
open_points.question: Which passage must change, or how can a close-delimited response whose decoded body has already reached the ceiling be distinguished from a longer response without reading at least one additional body byte?
